subject: Finova: Performance SLO & Regional routing follow-up

Subject: Finova discovery — performance SLOs & regional routing (post-call recap)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of the key items we discussed and agreed actions so we can stay aligned: 

1) Goals and constraints
- Finova target: conversational workflows serving customers in US/EU/APAC with consistent UX.
- Must meet region-specific latency SLOs for end-user interactions and keep EU customer data resident in EU.

2) Performance / SLO targets you called out (confirmed during call)
- Interactive chat (streaming): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 150ms (US); p95 < 180ms (EU); p95 < 250ms (APAC)
- Throughput: baseline 300 requests/sec across global footprint, with peak bursts to 900 rps for short windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions ~120, but 95th percentile concurrency per instance ~60; we should plan for headroom.
- Streaming: server-sent events (token-by-token) required for the customer-facing UI; need sub-200ms time-to-first-token in US/EU.

3) Routing & data residency
- Route EU traffic to EU cluster and persist EU customer data only in EU (data-at-rest).
- APAC traffic should prefer Tokyo region; US traffic prefer us-west-2.
- For regulated workflows we discussed dedicated pools (Dedicated plan) vs hosted with geo-fencing.

4) Next steps / asks from Redwood
- Aditya: share recommended instance sizing, concurrency model, and a proposed test plan (24h synthetic load + streaming checks).
- Marissa: provide a mutual action plan and tentative timeline for a proof-of-concept (POC) + decision criteria.
- Alice / Finova: send current traffic shape (histogram by region, peak days) and any network egress/ingress constraints.

Attachments: please see the template SLO spreadsheet I dropped in the Drive link (copied below). I attached a short template (finova-slo-requirements.xlsx) for you to fill with more precise numbers if you have them.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute technical sync next week to review Aditya's test plan and pick the POC window. I put suggested slots in the calendar invite — please accept what works.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Alice / team — quick technical reply to the p95 / routing question and proposed test plan.

Short answer on EU p95 < 180ms with streaming: yes, with the following configuration and assumptions.

Assumptions / recommended config:
- Model: optimized 1.3B variant with quantized weights for lower latency.
- Dedicated regional pools: provision Dedicated GPU pools in EU-west-1 and us-west-2; APAC on tokyo-1. Dedicated pools reduce noisy neighbor risk and improve tail latency.
- Autoscale headroom: reserve concurrency headroom of 2x (target concurrency 120 -> reserve capacity for 240) to absorb bursts.
- Network: customer edge -> nearest Redwood region; we recommend colocating a small edge proxy in Finova's network if you need sub-200ms TTFT at p95 in APAC.

Performance targets we can commit to for the POC (subject to final topology and model choice):
- US (us-west-2): p50 ~45–60ms, p95 < 120–150ms, TTFT <120ms for streaming.
- EU (eu-west-1): p50 ~60–80ms, p95 < 150–180ms, TTFT <160–180ms for streaming.
- APAC (ap-northeast-1): p50 ~90–120ms, p95 < 200–250ms, TTFT <200–250ms depending on Finova edge routing.

Throughput & concurrency
- Baseline: test config will be 300 rps sustained, with 30-minute bursts to 900 rps. We will validate autoscaling response times and queueing latency.
- Concurrency: we will simulate 150 concurrent sessions (token-streaming enabled) and measure p95 tail latency.

Proposed POC test plan (high-level)
1) Pre-test: exchange firewall IPs and a signed confidentiality addendum for test data.
2) 24-hour soak: sustained 300 rps across regions, validate p50/p95 and streaming TTFT.
3) Burst tests: 3 x 30-minute bursts to 900 rps to validate autoscale and fallback policies.
4) Regression checks: verify responses and sampling for quality drift.

We will share a runnable test script (k6 + streaming harness), expected instance types, and monitoring dashboards. After the soak we can produce a short runbook with tuning recommendations (batch size, KV cache warmup, quantization profile).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla-datasheet.pdf (summary SLA and dedicated pool options).

If this aligns, Marissa — can you lock a 30-minute slot Thu or Fri for the technical sync?

Thanks,
